subQuestions.questionText: The relative location of one place in relation to another place is referred to as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (situation) (1 mark)
Situation refers to the relative location of a place in relation to its surroundings or to another place, whereas site refers to the actual ground on which a settlement is built.

subQuestions.questionText: The economic sector and economic function that dominate in rural settlements can be described as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (primary and unifunctional) (1 mark)
Rural settlements are dominated by primary activities (e.g. farming, mining, forestry) and usually perform a single (unifunctional) function.

subQuestions.questionText: The type of settlement illustrated below is a … (refer to the sketch in the question paper).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (wet-point settlement) (1 mark)
A wet-point settlement locates where water is readily available (e.g. at a spring, river or water source), as illustrated in the sketch.

subQuestions.questionText: Settlements along the coast generally have a … shape.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (semi-circular) (1 mark)
Settlements located along a coastline are restricted by the sea on one side and therefore develop a semi-circular shape around the coast.

subQuestions.questionText: The land-use model below can be identified as a multiple nuclei model because it has … (refer to the sketch in the question paper).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (many focal points) (1 mark)
The multiple nuclei model is characterised by several separate nuclei or focal points around which land-use zones develop, rather than a single centre.

subQuestions.questionText: The … refers to the number of people required for a business to make a profit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (threshold population) (1 mark)
The threshold population is the minimum number of people required to support a business or service so that it can operate profitably.

subQuestions.questionText: The urban area below is … shaped (refer to the sketch in the question paper).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (linear) (1 mark)
The sketch shows the urban area developed in a line (e.g. along a route or valley), which is the defining feature of a linear shape.

subQuestions.questionText: Urbanisation refers to the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (percentage by which urban populations increase) (1 mark)
Urbanisation refers to the increase in the percentage of people living in urban areas relative to rural areas.

options.A: decreasing number of people that live in rural areas.
options.B: physical growth of an urban area.
options.C: percentage by which urban populations increase.

subQuestions.questionText: Select ONE term/concept from the list (hamlet; town; megalopolis; isolated farmstead; conurbation; village; city; metropolis) for the description: A settlement that is the smallest in a hierarchy.

subQuestions.memoText: Megalopolis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain why rural migrants experience difficulty in finding employment in area B and the impact thereof on their quality of life.

subQuestions.questionText: The GDP is the total value of …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (goods and services produced within a country in one year) (1 mark)
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total value of all goods and services produced within the borders of a country in one year.

options.A: goods and services produced within a country in one year.
options.B: goods and services produced by permanent citizens in one year.
options.C: exports that leave a country in one year.
options.D: imports that come into a country in one year.

subQuestions.questionText: The concept … is used to refer to products sold within South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (home market) (1 mark)
The home market refers to the sale of products within the country (locally), i.e. within South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Food security occurs when …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (there is access to sufficient nutritious food) (1 mark)
Food security exists when all people have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food.

options.A: there is a lack of food that gives rise to starvation.
options.B: there is access to sufficient nutritious food.
options.C: farmers experience drought and crop diseases.

subQuestions.questionText: … is a physical factor that affects food security in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Rainfall) (1 mark)
Rainfall is a physical (natural) factor affecting food security, whereas research, trade and HIV/Aids are human factors.

subQuestions.questionText: TWO types of industries associated with bulk transport: (i) Ubiquitous (ii) Heavy (iii) Light (iv) Raw-material orientated.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((ii) and (iv)) (1 mark)
Heavy industries and raw-material orientated industries handle large, bulky raw materials and products and are therefore associated with bulk transport.

subQuestions.questionText: TWO types of industries generally associated with lower levels of air pollution: (i) Ubiquitous (ii) Heavy (iii) Light (iv) Raw-material orientated.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C ((i) and (iii)) (1 mark)
Ubiquitous and light industries produce small consumer goods and are generally associated with lower levels of air pollution.

subQuestions.questionText: … is an example of a tertiary activity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (Transport) (1 mark)
Transport is a service and therefore a tertiary activity. Mining is primary, and motor vehicle assembly is secondary.

subQuestions.questionText: … refers to the difference in value between imports and exports.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (Balance of trade) (1 mark)
The balance of trade is the difference in value between a country's imports and exports.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to spot height 1738, F in block B1 and windpump, G in block B3 on the topographic map. The rough cross-section between spot height 1738 and the windpump is … (choose the correct cross-section sketch A, B, C or D).

subQuestions.questionText: What is the difference in height between spot height 1738 and the windpump?

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the distance between the spot height 1738 and the windpump in metres. Formula: Actual Distance = Map distance x Map scale.
subQuestions.memoText:
Actual Distance = Map distance x Map scale
Actual Distance = 5,5 cm (Range 5,4 – 5,6) (1) x 500 m
= 2 750 m (Range 2 700 – 2 800 m) (1)
(2 x 1 = 2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Use the answers to QUESTIONS 3.1.4 and 3.1.5 to calculate the average gradient between spot height 1738 and the windpump. Formula: Average gradient = Vertical interval (VI) / Horizontal equivalent (HE).
subQuestions.memoText:
Average gradient = Vertical interval (VI) / Horizontal equivalent (HE)
Average Gradient = 38 / 2 750
= 38/38 : 2 750/38
= 1 : 72,36 (1) (Range 1:71,05 – 1:73,68)
(2 x 1 = 2 marks)
NOTE: If answers for 3.1.4 and 3.1.5 are incorrect but are substituted correctly in 3.1.6, a mark should be allocated for this.
